item.title: 2 more rescued from debris in Nepal 10 days after devastating floods
item.description: The rescue brings the total to three workers saved from a hydropower tunnel, after two other workers were freed a day before.

item.title: U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for Iran targeting warships
item.description: Iran fired ballistic missiles at a U.S. aircraft carrier and a destroyer, but the ships were able to evade the attacks, Central Command said.

item.title: Passenger duct taped to seat after allegedly calling flight attendant racial slur
item.description: A passenger on an American Airlines flight was duct-taped to a seat after he allegedly used a racial slur against a flight attendant and punched a fellow passenger.

item.title: Painting looted by Nazis to be returned to collector's heir
item.description: The painting was among the artworks looted and sold under duress to Nazi officials from art dealer Jacques Goudstikker after Adolf Hitler's Germany invaded the Netherlands in 1940.

item.title: Witkoff, Kushner visit Moscow in latest push to end war in Ukraine
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered a three-day halt in Russian strikes on Kyiv during the U.S. envoys' visit to the Ukrainian capital, the Kremlin said.

item.title: A woman was in pain for decades. A chance meeting helped her learn why.
item.description: Dawn Jemison started dealing with pelvic pain as a preteen. It took decades to learn why — and to find a solution.

item.title: Top military officials faced polygraphs over leaks on munitions, sources say
item.description: Some of the highest-ranking officials in the U.S. military were subjected to polygraph tests as part of a sweeping leak probe, U.S. officials briefed on the matter told CBS News.

item.title: After Lindsay Clancy mistrial, what happens next?
item.description: Here's what may happen next after a mistrial was declared in Lindsay Clancy's murder case.

item.title: Clancy trial ends in hung jury after attorney's attempt to avoid mistrial fails
item.description: A mistrial was declared in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial Friday, after her attorney's last-minute appeal failed.

item.title: Fetterman texts reveal impatience with constituent duties
item.description: A former staffer confirmed that Sen. John Fetterman has routinely dismissed and at times refused to do core aspects of the job.

item.title: Serena and Venus Williams fall in thriller return to U.S. Open women's doubles
item.description: Playing together at the U.S. Open in New York for the first time in four years, Serena​ and Venus Williams lost in a three-set thriller match in the first round of the women's doubles tournament.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 6)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Barry Morphew arrested, booked into Boulder County Jail
item.description: Barry Morphew is back behind bars after a judge granted prosecutors' request for an arrest warrant.

item.title: Senior aides to U.K.'s Nigel Farage step down in scandal over undercover report
item.description: Two senior aides to Nigel Farage, the firebrand leader of the U.K.'s populist Reform party, have stepped down in the wake of an investigative news report.

item.title: Nigel Farage's Reform U.K. accused of breaking foreign funding law after undercover investigation
item.description: Reform U.K.'s annual convention comes amid fresh controversy after an undercover investigation alleged that senior figures in Nigel Farage's party discussed securing foreign funding, which is prohibited under British law. Reform denies wrongdoing, saying it was the victim of a hoax. CBS News reporter Inaya Folarin Iman has the details.

item.title: FBI using AI to zero in on threats faster, deputy director says
item.description: FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia says the bureau is turning to artificial intelligence as a tool to identify threats and act on them faster.

item.title: New movies to look out for this fall
item.description: The fall movie season is here. Variety senior entertainment writer Angelique Jackson joins CBS News to preview some of the films coming out over the next few months.

item.title: FBI deputy director explains how agency is using AI to fight crime
item.description: The FBI is using artificial intelligence to fight crime as it leans into targeting cartels and transnational criminal organizations. CBS News' Anna Schecter spoke with FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia about the new technology.

item.title: Neighborhood comes together to give young boy a memorable trick-or-treat birthday
item.description: When a mother posted a note on Facebook asking if anyone in her neighborhood would allow her son to trick-or-treat at their homes in July for his 11th birthday, more than 100 neighbors said yes.

item.title: Beyoncé celebrates birthday by dropping "B-Day" 20th anniversary deluxe edition
item.description: Beyoncé is celebrating her birthday on Friday by dropping a 20th anniversary edition of her defining album, "B'Day." SiriusXM Radio host Lamar Dawson joins CBS News with a look at Queen Bey's album and other pop culture news.

item.title: NFL demands Kalshi and Polymarket refrain from offering questionable sports bets
item.description: The NFL is demanding that prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket stop offering risky bets that can be easily influenced by one person. Mark Strassman has the story.

item.title: Global warming set to cross threshold sooner than expected, U.N. report finds
item.description: In a new report, officials with the United Nations say the world is close to crossing the global warming temperature threshold sooner than expected. Kristie Ebi, one of the lead authors, joins CBS News to discuss the findings.

item.title: American Airlines passenger duct-taped to seat after mid-flight outburst
item.description: A picture shows the man with multiple loops of tape around his wrists, torso and head.

item.title: Witkoff, Kushner to visit Moscow and Kyiv in renewed push to end Russia-Ukraine war
item.description: The Trump administration is trying to revive peace talks between Russia and Ukraine. This weekend, White House special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner are traveling to Moscow and Kyiv to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. John Herbst, former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine and Uzbekistan, joins with analysis.

item.title: Construction of 250-feet-tall "Arc de Trump" set to begin in D.C.
item.description: Construction of President Trump's 250-feet-tall triumphal arch, nicknamed the "Arc de Trump," is set to begin in Washington, D.C. Weijia Jiang has more.

item.title: Judge extends block on Postal Service's new Trump-backed mail-in ballot requirements
item.description: A federal judge extended her block on the U.S. Postal Service's new requirements for mail voting, as states prepare to begin sending mail ballots to voters for the November midterm elections.

item.title: 9/4: CBS Evening News
item.description: What Lindsay Clancy mistrial ruling means; Storms, heat waves cause Labor Day disruption.

item.title: Judge lets Pentagon move forward with firing Stars and Stripes journalists
item.description: The Pentagon accused two of the Stars and Stripes journalists of insubordination after one of them had told "CBS Sunday Morning" in a July interview that she worked for Stars and Stripes, "not for the Pentagon, not for any administration, not for any policymaker."

item.title: Is a far-right party on the precipice of power in a German state?
item.description: AfD Saxony-Anhalt is a racist extremist group, according to the German state's intelligence agency. The party may well trounce its rivals in this weekend's state election.

item.title: Work on Trump-backed triumphal arch will start in coming weeks
item.description: The federal government plans to start excavation over the next two weeks on a massive triumphal arch near Washington, D.C., Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum said, a controversial project championed by President Trump.
